Chapter 4
The LOKLOK Platform: Architecture and
Implementation
Chapter abstract. This chapter describes LOKLOK: the Broadcaster Reputation
Score, MORE diversity-constrained recommendation, propaganda detection and mod-
eration, the ERIC governance loop, and the measurement surface. It presents the eld
interface and explains how BRS, credibility intervals, the Echo Meter, and the sur-
vey ow appeared to participants. It separates implemented mechanisms from claims
about deployment and usage.
LOKLOK is the proposed operational platform for this research programme.
Its implementation account describes a Go backend, mobile client, and web inter-
face. The following chapter distinguishes proposed reference mechanisms, reported
implementation behavior, and requirements for experimental delity. Neither a plat-
form feature nor a mathematical analogy establishes an EST proposition without a
suitable test.

4.3
Recommendation with Diversity Constraints (MORE)
The Multi-Objective Recommendation Engine ranks candidate content by a
weighted combination of user value and diversity, subject to a fairness budget.
User value combines the propaganda-adjusted probability of the item with the
broadcaster's BRS:
UVS(c, u) = PDTS(c, u) · Bc · (1 −Pprop(c)).
(4.4)
In plain terms.
The utility score ranks candidate broadcasts by expected value,
diversity, and a penalty term. It is the app's "what should I show next" rule.
4.3.1
Time-Resolved Attentional Coherence: A Zewail-Inspired Formal
Analogy
The quantity PDTS(c, u) in Equation (4.4) requires an explicit denition. A com-
muter with the radio application running is not necessarily attending to the broad-
cast: the phone may be playing in the background while the rider talks, checks
messages, or watches trac. The present framework therefore treats attention as a
time-resolved coupling state between a listener u and a broadcast c, rather than as
a synonym for ride duration or application presence.
The formal inspiration is Ahmed H. Zewail's femtochemistry, recognised by

CHAPTER 4. THE LOKLOK PLATFORM: ARCHITECTURE AND
IMPLEMENTATION
64
the 1999 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. In pumpprobe spectroscopy, a pump pulse
launches a coherent wavepacket at t0; a delayed probe pulse measures the transition-
state population at t0 +∆t before vibrational dephasing destroys coherence (Zewail,
1999, 2000). The analogy used here is deliberately formal: it supplies a principled
way to model a short-lived attentional window, not a claim that social listening
obeys physical thermodynamics or chemical kinetics.
Let tpump be the timestamp of a broadcast inection cue (a claim assertion,
a topic shift, or a source prompt), and let tprobe = tpump + ∆tu,c be the listener's
foreground interaction, telemetry ping, or EMA Layer-1 response. The pumpprobe
attentional coherence gate is

where τdephase,u > 0 is the listener's dephasing time, Edistract is ambient transit
friction (trac noise, multi-tasking, conversation), Tcog is the listener's cognitive en-
gagement energy, and ∆ϕu,c(t) is the phase dierence between the broadcast cadence
and the listener's foreground focus. The gate lies in [0, 1]: an active, phase-locked
listener probed within the coherence window has PDTS →1; a phone left playing in
the background for several minutes has PDTS →0. The numerical values used in the
simulation are declared design parameters, not measured chemical quantities.
In plain terms. The gate is a formal way to say three common-sense things. First,
attention fades as time passes. Second, a noisy or distracting ride lowers attention.
Third, attention is stronger when the broadcast rhythm and the listener focus are

gram is a formal analogy: the broadcast inection cue is the pump, the EMA probe
is the delayed measurement, and dephasing represents loss of foreground attention
during a ride. It is not a claim that social listening is a chemical process.
The gate enters the model in three places. First, it multiplies the retention
term in the broadcaster-rigour update so that passive background play cannot in-

reputation update. Third, it modulates engagement and the latent credibility tra-
jectory. Figure 4.2 shows the resulting decay curves and the active-versus-passive
contrast. The implementation is included in loklok_pipeline.py (Section K), so
the analogy is auditable rather than purely rhetorical.

4.4
Propaganda Detection and Algorithmic Moderation
Every content item is scored on seven features: citation velocity, quality-weighted
entropy, semantic fear bias, propagation acceleration, institutional concentration
(HHI), predatory-source ratio, and correction velocity.
The specication uses a
logistic score, ˆp(c) = σ(θ⊤f(c)), and combines it with a temporal anomaly score. A
logistic transformation alone does not establish probability calibration; a separate
calibration dataset and assessment would be needed before describing the output as
calibrated. The proposed combined index is
Pprop(c) = 0.7 ˆp(c) + 0.3 ϕTIS(c).
(4.7)
If Pprop > 0.70 the item receives a visibility penalty, an applied Moderation Cost
Ea,mod = λ1(Pprop −0.70) embedded in the feed rank. This is a proposed ranking
penalty, not an established economic welfare correction or a calibrated probability
of intent. The anomaly score must also be bounded on [0, 1] for the combined index
to remain in that range. These author-dened thresholds require evaluation. If the
score exceeds 0.85 the item is escalated to ERIC for human review and the broadcast

CHAPTER 4. THE LOKLOK PLATFORM: ARCHITECTURE AND
IMPLEMENTATION
69
logs a BRS information-quality penalty.
4.5
The ERIC Governance Loop
ERIC is the platform's integrity controller. It monitors ve health indicators (lter-
bubble score, information diversity, inequality of reputation, detection accuracy,
platform sentiment) and selects the minimum-cost intervention, a diversity injec-
tion, a friction pause, or a human review, whenever a threshold is crossed. The
intended decision rule is to compare changes in a specied governance objective,
with its components, scales, and costs recorded. A decrease in the candidate Hamil-
tonian is not by itself evidence of improved credibility or factual accuracy. Any
use of the entropy-regularised objective must separately dene the loss and source
distribution, as in Appendix E. An anti-bot module assigns cryptographic identi-
ties, monitors behavioural ngerprints, and ags coordination patterns (Luceri et
al., 2023); its output feeds the reputation and moderation subsystems rather than
making autonomous removal decisions.
4.6
Measurement Surface
The platform specication includes the following measurement services. They de-
scribe the wider design, not a claim that every service was used in the present
cross-sectional survey. In particular, the eld sample is not a session-randomised
trial, and no weekly or pre-broadcast panel results are added by describing these
capabilities:
 Layer 1  Post-broadcast micro-survey (PB1PB5): red within sec-

 Layer 3  Weekly survey (WK1WK15): longitudinal trust and media-

 Layer 4  Pre-broadcast condence survey (PR1PR3): broadcaster-

 Experiment arms: a random 50/50 assignment places each session into an
epistemic-rst (G1) or engagement-rst (G0) conguration, with the assign-

 BRS and echo cards: the Flutter and SPA clients render the BRS point

The full item text of every layer is given in Appendix A.
4.7

The historical implementation account describes a Go backend, a static web client,
a mobile client design, and supporting services. Their source trees, test logs, and
deployment records are not included in the present archive. This version therefore
makes no fresh claim about source-le counts, passing tests, live routes, or feature
completeness. The mechanism equations are specications, not proof that a deployed

4.8
Domain Model and Data Flow
The following entities describe a proposed shared schema for the platform and model.
They do not establish that the historical engine and actual backend use identical data
transformations. The core entities are: User (identity, career phase, institution);
Broadcaster (a user with a BRS trajectory); Broadcast (session, schedule slot,
transcript embedding, source list); Rating (the post-broadcast micro-survey and
star record); EchoSample (the Echo Meter rolling values and EMA trigger history);
and GovernanceEvent (moderation, anti-bot, and ERIC ledger records).
The
intended experimental event ow connects assignment, content exposure, rating,
feedback, and logged outcomes. In the supplied source these are separate routes
and services, not a demonstrated end-to-end G0/G1 experiment.
Per-user A/B
assignment and the radio service's shared current arm are separate states. The feed
ranking path does not read the stored assignment. Consequently, assignment alone
does not establish that a user received the intended intervention. The proposed study
identies treatment by both the assigned conguration and recorded exposures, with
